    Early in the second quarter Wednesday night in NBA Cup group play, LeBron James pulled up from Broad Street.

    He drilled a 35-foot 3-pointer amid a torrid stretch that saw him make a trio of triples and score 14 straight points for the 76ers on Thanksgiving Eve. Before that sequence, the Sixers were trailing the Miami Heat by three points at Philadelphia's Xfinity Mobile Arena. Afterward, they were up eight.

    Industry observers note that while becoming the oldest player in NBA history to notch a triple double — at 41 years and 330 days old — James continued his recent hot streak from beyond the arc, going 4 of 6 on 3-point attempts. Philadelphia shot 14 of 35 from long range en route to a 111-104 victory.

    The Heat (10-7) would have clinched East Group B had they come out on top, but Philadelphia (15-4) denied Miami an eighth consecutive win, despite losing Jaylen Brown to a hamstring injury late in the first half and Joel Embiid being sidelined by illness.

    Nick Nurse's squad is now 2-1 in NBA Cup competition; Erik Spoelstra's Heat dropped to that same mark.

    It has been revealed that james finished with a season-high 25 points and 12 assists, plus 10 rebounds, with maybe his most notable dime taking place early in the fourth quarter. The 22-time All-Star highlighted his elite court vision, timing a halfcourt lob perfectly to connect with VJ Edgecombe for a layup. James later dialed up an alley-oop for forward Dominick Barlow to throw down.

    Edgecombe was among the Sixers players stepping up in the absence of Brown and Embiid, as Philadelphia protected its nine-point halftime lead and kept Miami at arm's length over the final two quarters. He had 18 points, and Tyrese Maxey poured in 30.

    The Heat, who wound up trailing by 16 late in the final frame, were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, who clocked out with 32 points, 14 rebounds and 4 assists.

    Kevin Durant is now one of five NBA players to score 33,000 points. The 38-year-old Houston Rockets forward achieved that feat on Wednesday night in a 116-104 home victory against the Phoenix Suns. He joined James, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Karl Malone and Kobe Bryant.

    Durant did so while piling up 20 points for Houston (14-5), which, despite already being eliminated from NBA Cup knockout-round contention, kept pace in the upper echelon of the Western Conference standings.

    In a recent development, the Rockets improved to 2-2 in Cup group play, while the Suns (9-8) slid to 1-2. They, too, have been eliminated from knockout-round contention in West Group A.

    Industry observers note that along the way, Houston center Alperen Şengün passed Hakeem Olajuwon for the second-most triple-doubles in franchise history. Şengün, only 24 years old, secured his 15th performance of that kind with 23 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists.

    Late in the game, Suns wing Dillon Brooks got into it with Durant and was ejected after receiving his second technical foul of the night.

    Although the Minnesota Timberwolves lost LaMelo Ball to an ankle injury Wednesday, they held on to defeat the Oklahoma City Thunder 113-106.

    Industry observers note that jaden McDaniels came through, substantial time, in the West Group B matchup. In fact, by game's end, he was the third player in Wolves history to log at least 30 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists in consecutive games. That elite firm also includes Karl-Anthony Towns and Kevin Garnett.

    After going for 34 points, 10 rebounds and 6 assists on Monday in a win over the Brooklyn Nets, McDaniels put up 32 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists this time out versus the Thunder (10-9), who are 2-7 in their last nine games and eliminated from Cup knockout-round contention.

    Minnesota (14-5), on the other hand, is atop West Group B with a 3-0 record. McDaniels beat the third-quarter buzzer with a ridiculous off-balance shot. A late 3-pointer from Wolves guard Ayo Dosunmu helped seal the deal.

    In a recent development, all gold mining stocks present a relatively high level of risk. The price of gold vacillates wildly. The precious metal hit an all-time high of $5,589.38 per ounce at the end of January but is now trading at around $3,572 per ounce.

    Industry observers note that it's cost-intensive to run a mining tech giant, and even when gold prices are rising, operational costs and debt loads can easily outweigh a company's profit potential. Agnico Eagle Mines and Franco-Nevada both mitigate those risks, but in substantially different ways.

    According to recent reports, agnico Eagle's gold mines present less jurisdictional risk from geopolitical and labor disruptions than typical gold mining stocks. The tech giant operates in Tier-1 mining-friendly locations, including Canada, Australia, Finland, and Mexico.

    Agnico also hasn't had to make expensive acquisitions of late thanks to continued underground expansion at its Canadian Malartic location and project growth at Hope Bay in Nunavut, Canada, and at Ikkari in Finland.

    In a recent development, in the third quarter, the manufacturer reported nine-month all-in sustaining costs (AISC) of $1,529 per ounce of gold while selling each ounce for an average of $4,537. Agnico reported nine-month earnings per share (EPS) of $9.25, up 58% year over year.     NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    The firm also raised its dividend by 12.5% this year to $0.45 per share quarterly, yielding around 1.11% at its current share price, which is right around the S&P 500 average. The cash dividend payout ratio is only 19.3%, so it is more than well-covered.

    Recent findings suggest that franco-Nevada is a gold streaming company. It doesn't actually mine for gold but earns royalties from the gold-mining companies to which it has provided up-front funds. When gold prices rise, the company benefits either from royalty payments or the right to purchase a portion of the mine's gold production at a pre-agreed-upon discounted price, known as a stream.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    It has been revealed that the company has interests in 445 assets, including 129 operating mines. Most of its money comes from gold mining, roughly 70%, though it also makes money from natural gas liquids, oil, gas, and silver.

    Because it only needs a handful of employees -- 44 full-time and five part-time contractors, as of the end of 2025 -- to operate, its margins are higher than typical mining companies.

    In a recent development, through nine months, the company reported EPS of $6.30, up 63.1% year over year, and record revenue of $1.78 billion, up 45% over the same period a year ago. Like Agnico Eagle, its dividend is well-covered, with a cash dividend payout ratio of only 26.3%.

However, if the stock market declines sharply, rather than raising rates, the Federal Reserve would likely lower them, making gold more attractive.

    In the meantime, Agnico Eagle and Franco-Nevada are financially healthy and more stable than most mining stocks, with safe dividends.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    S&P 500 Sell-Off: Here's Why I'm Not Panicking -- and What I'm Doing Instead

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (834 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Monday was a great example of why investors shouldn't panic sell during a correction or significant market downturn.
    • 20, the Nasdaq had been in near bear market territory, down 18% from its all-time high of 27,599 on Oct.
    • If you did sell shares in a Nasdaq or tech-focused ETF, or a stock like Nvidia, which gained some 30% on the day alone after CEO Jensen Huang was rehired, you would have lost out on a huge return.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Dave Kovaleski – Nov 26, 2026 at 10:45AM EST.

    Monday was a great example of why investors shouldn't panic sell during a correction or significant market downturn. On Nov. 23, the S&P 500 jumped nearly 5%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 3% and the Nasdaq Composite had one of its best days ever, rising 1,471 points, or 6.5%.

    Sources indicate that as of Nov. 20, the Nasdaq had been in near bear market territory, down 18% from its all-time high of 27,599 on Oct. 6. But on Nov. 23, with its nearly 1,500-point gain, it surged to 24,089. It is still down 12% from Oct. 6, and there may be volatile days ahead, but days like Monday are one reason you don't want to panic sell during a downturn.

    If you did sell shares in a Nasdaq or tech-focused ETF, or a stock like Nvidia, which gained some 30% on the day alone after CEO Jensen Huang was rehired, you would have lost out on a huge return.

    Industry observers note that and it's just not a one-off type scenario that won't ever happen again. There are stats to show how much it can negatively impact your portfolio when you miss the market's best days during the correction of a bear market.

    Image source: OpenAI (AI-generated illustration).

    Earlier this year, the Hartford Funds released a report that examined this very subject. It found that from 1950 through 2025, 76% of the market's best days were either during a bear market or within the first two months of a bull market. Of that, 48% came during a bear market. We're not yet in a bear market, but that could certainly change in the months ahead.

    Recent findings suggest that the Hartford report also compiled some numbers on how missing out on the best days would affect a long-term portfolio. It revealed that $10,000 invested in the S&P 500 in 1996 would grow to $192,167 after 30 years, through 2025, based on the average annual total returns of the S&P 500.

    If you missed the market's 10 best days, that would bring it down to $85,490. If you missed the best 20 days, the total would be $49,551. If you missed the market's best 30 days, you'd have $31,123 -- 84% less than if you stayed fully invested all 30 years.

    According to recent reports, fidelity did a similar study in August, putting a slightly finer point on it. It looks at the impact of missing the market's best days since 1988. A $10,000 investment in the S&P 500 from Jan. 1, 1988 to Dec. 31, 2025 would generate $616,013. Missing just the five best days would result in 38% less in your portfolio, about $380,479.

    There are a few things to understand that should help guide you through bear markets and rough patches.

    Sources indicate that one, understand that bear markets do not last as long as bull markets, nor do they have a bigger net effect on your portfolio. A study by the Hartford Funds also found that there have been 27 bear markets since 1928 and 28 bull markets. The average length of a bear market is 289 days, while the average bull market lasts 988 days. Further, the Hartford Funds research highlighted that stocks lose 35% on average in a bear market and gain 112% on average in a bull market.

    Two, over the past 30 years, the S&P 500 has averaged a 14.4% annualized total return, while the Nasdaq has averaged a 17.2% return. That's through the dot-com bust, the Great Recession, the COVID bear market, and the 2022 bear market. So, patience has been rewarded over the years.

    And three, downturns and bear markets are a great time to buy, not sell. Many good companies with strong fundamentals in market-leading positions get caught up in negative waves. When that happens, it is time to buy these great stocks at discounts.

    According to recent reports, in general, downturns are an opportune time to review your holdings. While there may be great buys out there in a bear market, you may also see some stocks that are still overvalued, may be overleveraged, and may be facing industry or economic headwinds.

    The best thing to do is check their P/E ratios and valuation metrics, as well as their earnings outlooks. You may find the money invested in those stocks is put to better use in a broad ETF that tracks the Nasdaq or S&P 500 or one of the discount stocks you identified. This is how I approach downturns.

    #199731. Industry News: Meta Platforms Just Partnered With Walmart. Here's Why Investors Should Pay Attention

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Meta Platforms Just Partnered With Walmart. Here's Why Investors Should Pay Attention

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (794 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 11:05AM EST.
    • It has been revealed that one crucial debate between Meta Platforms' (META +3.40%) bulls and bears is whether the company's massive artificial intelligence (AI) spending is justified.
    • Recent findings suggest that that's a significant decline.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 11:05AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Meta Platforms ›.

    It has been revealed that one crucial debate between Meta Platforms' (META +3.40%) bulls and bears is whether the company's massive artificial intelligence (AI) spending is justified. The bears certainly have a point: The tech leader's free cash flow is declining, largely due to capex spending tied to its AI build-out. In the third quarter, Meta posted negative free cash flow of $2.1 billion, compared with positive free cash flow of $10.6 billion in the year-ago quarter.

    Recent findings suggest that that's a significant decline. However, Meta Platforms' AI-related initiatives are slowly taking shape, and a recent partnership with Walmart (WMT -0.28%) highlights the opportunity ahead for the organization.

    First, let's back up a little. Meta Platforms released its Muse AI agent to the public in early September. It quickly became one of the most downloaded iOS apps. Meta later released several other versions of Muse, including one for small businesses. Management noted on the company's third-quarter earnings call that 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up Muse within a month and a half of its release. The tech giant also mentioned that 25% of those who had set up Muse used it daily, and growth remained strong.

    According to recent reports, but how does Meta plan to monetize Muse? The AI agent offers subscriptions for people who want higher usage capabilities (the base version is free). But Meta is targeting a potentially more lucrative opportunity. It plans to charge retailers transaction fees every time Muse helps a consumer make a purchase. That brings us to the company's partnership with Walmart. Meta Platforms and Walmart have partnered to integrate Muse with Walmart's e-commerce infrastructure through the retailer's Agent Gateway.

    According to recent reports, the integration allows consumers to use Muse to discover products, compare prices, find deals, and complete purchases on their behalf, subject to user-defined permissions and spending limits. While the precise financial details of this deal were not disclosed, Meta could earn commission fees for transactions Muse helps facilitate.

    Walmart is one of the largest retailers in the world, so this partnership is an key one for Meta. It could also help increase Muse's adoption. Some retailers are hesitant to get on board because they fear it will disrupt their business models and undermine their ability to protect customer relationships, as Meta's CFO, Susan Li, said.

    Recent findings suggest that this may happen if agents like Muse become the primary shopping interface -- instead of visiting a retailer's website, consumers could ask an agent to compare prices, quality, and other factors across many retailers, thereby potentially reducing retailers' direct relationships with consumers. Even so, consumers' adoption will largely determine where this market is headed.

    Industry observers note that if Muse can continue gaining users, a significant percentage of them use the agent to make purchases, and at least some retailers start adapting to the change -- as Walmart is doing -- that could force other retailers to follow suit. Eventually, Meta could generate significant sales from transaction fees.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Of course, Meta's core advertising business remains healthy. In the third quarter, the organization's revenue increased by 26% year over year to $64.6 billion. It also ended the period with 3.64 billion daily active people, an increase of 3% year over year. Meta's AI-powered algorithms across its websites and apps have helped grow engagement.

    Recent findings suggest that as CEO Mark Zuckerberg pointed out, Facebook and Instagram are hitting near all-time highs in engagement, and Threads -- Meta's competitor to X (formerly Twitter) -- has overtaken X in monthly actives. The point is that even before we look at Meta's opportunity with Muse, the company's underlying business looks strong. It's also worth noting that building the capacity required to support an agent like Muse requires substantial upfront investments.

    Meta is dishing out that money today, but the manufacturer's expenses in this area should decrease over time, and as Muse gains traction, revenue growth, profits, margins, and free cash flow could jump. Lastly, Meta is trading at 16.3x forward earnings, which, in my view, is more than fair, considering the company's robust underlying business and long-term opportunities in advertising and AI.

    #199711. Industry News: Hedge funds are no longer just for the rich. They’re wooing everyday investors

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1116 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Hedge funds are no longer just for the rich. They’re wooing everyday investors

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1116 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For decades, hedge funds were the preserve of billionaires, pension funds and deep-pocketed institutional investors.
    • The shift, dubbed by some as the "retailization" of hedge funds, comes as alternative asset managers seek new avenues for growth and investors look for ways to shield their portfolios from increasingly volatile equity markets.
    • Unlike traditional equity funds, which typically rely on stocks rising to generate returns, hedge funds can employ strategies including short selling, arbitrage and derivatives to seek profits across different market conditions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    For decades, hedge funds were the preserve of billionaires, pension funds and deep-pocketed institutional investors. Now, the industry is increasingly courting a new pool of capital: everyday investors.

    The shift, dubbed by some as the "retailization" of hedge funds, comes as alternative asset managers seek new avenues for growth and investors look for ways to shield their portfolios from increasingly volatile equity markets.

    Unlike traditional equity funds, which typically rely on stocks rising to generate returns, hedge funds can employ strategies including short selling, arbitrage and derivatives to seek profits across different market conditions.

    For an industry already managing record levels of assets, individual investors represent a largely untapped growth opportunity, experts who spoke to CNBC stated.

    Industry observers note that "Hedge funds are entrepreneurs. Their objective is to make as much money as they possibly can, both in returns and for their organization," stated Don Steinbrugge, CEO of hedge fund consulting firm Agecroft Partners.

    "So if they have the ability to go after a new market and grow their business, they're going to do that.".

    The push is coming from both hedge fund managers seeking to broaden their investor base and traditional asset managers looking to capitalize on growing demand for alternative investments, said Ken Heinz, president of hedge fund research firm HFR.

    "Heightened geopolitical uncertainty, greater market volatility, inflation concerns, and the higher correlation between equities and bonds have raised questions about the effectiveness of conventional portfolio diversification," noted Ricky Siao, a hedge fund specialist at Swiss private bank UBP.

    The investment environment has become more challenging for investors who have historically relied on traditional allocations to equities and fixed income, he added.

    As a result, investors are increasingly seeking exposure to strategies such as arbitrage, event-driven investing and quantitative macro strategies to reduce their dependence on equity market returns.

    The democratization of hedge fund investing is taking shape through a growing array of investment vehicles, often with lower fees, smaller minimum investments and more frequent opportunities to withdraw money.

    Some of the biggest names in the hedge fund industry are already moving in that direction.

    Billionaire investor Bill Ackman's Pershing Square raised $5 billion in April for a publicly listed closed-end fund, giving everyday investors access to its investment expertise without the performance fees traditionally associated with hedge funds. The fund charges a 2% annual management fee.

    According to recent reports, british hedge fund giant Man Group, meanwhile, entered the U.S. ETF market last September and doubled its lineup to four actively managed funds just three months later.

    The broader shift is also changing how hedge fund strategies are packaged for individual investors.

    "What has changed most is the wrapper, not the strategy itself," stated Yi Ling Ong, managing partner and chief operating officer at Golden Horse Fund Management.

    In other words, hedge fund strategies are increasingly being packaged in more accessible vehicles such as mutual funds and ETFs, often with lower investment minimums and fewer restrictions on withdrawals.

    "Investors may still be getting exposure to long/short equity, credit, or macro strategies, but delivered through vehicles that offer quarterly or monthly liquidity and standardized reporting.".

    The trend is playing out across markets.

    In Europe, hedge fund managers have adapted strategies to fit regulated UCITS funds, which are accessible to individual investors. In the U.S., mutual funds and ETFs have similarly broadened access to alternative investment strategies.

    In Asia, digital wealth platforms are helping bridge the gap between institutional and individual investors.

    Singapore-based Endowus, which began offering hedge funds on its platform in 2022, has lowered minimum investments for semi-liquid funds to $50,000, while removing minimums altogether for some daily-liquid alternative funds, according to Chief Investment Officer Hugh Chung.

    While most hedge funds on the platform remain restricted to accredited investors, a growing number of alternative funds are becoming available to non-accredited investors, Chung said.

    India is seeing a similar shift through Specialized Investment Funds, or SIFs, which allow investors to access more sophisticated strategies through structures that more closely resemble traditional mutual funds, said Rajesh Singla of Alpha AMC.

    Assets under management in India's Specialized Investment Funds have more than quadrupled since March to 426.7 billion rupees as of end-October, according to data from the Association of Mutual Funds in India.

    The products carry a minimum investment of 1 million rupees, significantly below the entry thresholds typically associated with traditional hedge funds.

    The shift is also making hedge fund-style investing cheaper.

    Traditional hedge funds have long been associated with the "2 and 20" fee model, which typically charges a 2% annual management fee and taking 20% of investment profits.

    While those fees have come under pressure over the years, retail-friendly alternatives such as hedge fund-like ETFs typically charge a single annual management fee of between 0.4% and 1.25%, according to Ong.

    But lower fees does not necessarily mean better outcomes.

    Retail investment vehicles often face tighter regulatory and liquidity requirements, which can limit managers' ability to replicate strategies used by traditional hedge funds.

    Steinbrugge remarked those constraints can force managers to avoid less liquid securities that may offer some of the greatest opportunities for outsized returns.

    "What investors are really choosing between is not just price, but structure," Ong mentioned.

    The industry's expansion into the retail market is also raising questions about whether individual investors fully understand the complexity of the strategies they are buying into.

    Easier access does not eliminate the risks associated with leverage, short selling or illiquid investments.

    "The key risk is that investors may underestimate the complexity and risk associated with these strategies simply because they are now more accessible," Singla mentioned.

    Liquidity is another concern, particularly for less liquid alternative investments being marketed through retail-friendly structures.

    Some interval funds, which are increasingly being used to distribute private credit and other alternative investments to individuals, may offer to repurchase only 5% of their outstanding shares each quarter, Steinbrugge said.

    That could leave investors unable to withdraw as much money as they want during periods of market stress.

    Still, industry watchers largely see the rise of retail-friendly products as complementary to traditional hedge funds rather than an existential threat to them.

    While the proliferation of more liquid, transparent and lower-fee products could intensify competition and pressure traditional fee structures, Siao does not expect retailization to fundamentally reshape the industry in the foreseeable future.

    "I would expect this to be an incremental evolution rather than a fundamental transformation of the hedge fund business model," he mentioned.

    Recent findings suggest that "Over time, the industry will likely remain segmented," Ong remarked. "Retail vehicles will address accessibility and scale, while hedge funds will continue to focus on depth, flexibility, and outcomes that are difficult to replicate in simplified formats.".

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (411 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    South Korea upgrades growth forecast, raises benchmark rates to highest in two years

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (411 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • South Korea's central bank on Thursday hiked benchmark lending rates to their highest in two years, as inflation continues to run above target while a booming economy allows it room to tighten policy.
    • The central bank raised rates by 25 basis points to 3.25% for its final meeting of the year, in line with expectations from economists, data on the Bank of Korea's website showed.
    • Inflation is expected to remain above its 2% target level for a considerable time, the BOK added in its statement, saying this was due to the pass-through of elevated cost pressures and as demand-side pressures also gradually strengthen, driven by stronger economic growth.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    South Korea's central bank on Thursday hiked benchmark lending rates to their highest in two years, as inflation continues to run above target while a booming economy allows it room to tighten policy.

    The central bank raised rates by 25 basis points to 3.25% for its final meeting of the year, in line with expectations from economists, data on the Bank of Korea's website showed.

    Inflation is expected to remain above its 2% target level for a considerable time, the BOK added in its statement, saying this was due to the pass-through of elevated cost pressures and as demand-side pressures also gradually strengthen, driven by stronger economic growth. Inflation in the country stood at 2.8% in October.

    The BOK also upgraded its growth forecasts for 2026 to 3.9% for 2026 and 4.1% for 2027, up from the 3.3% and 2.9%, respectively, forecast in August.

    South Korea's third-quarter GDP grew by 3.4% year on year, beating expectations, allowing the central bank room to raise rates.

    "The projections of high growth rates for next year and beyond also reflect the significantly increasing weight of the IT sector as a growth engine for the Korean economy," BOK Governor Shin Hyun-song remarked at a press conference following the decision.

    Operating profits in the semiconductor sector could reach 700 trillion won, Shin told reporters, according to local news agency Yonhap.

    Shin also signaled that more rate hikes, although he did not give a fixed timeline.

    "While the domestic economy is expected to continue its robust growth, inflation is forecast to remain above the target level for a considerable time ... The Board, therefore, sees it warranted to continue its policy response until there is confidence that inflation will converge stably to the target level.".

    Gareth Leather, senior Asia Economist at Capital Economics noted there is reason to believe that the BOK's tightening cycle was drawing to a close.

    The BOK has raised rates by 75 basis points in five months, as higher energy prices from the Iran war and the AI boom has pushed up inflation in the country.

    Leather noted that the country's strong growth, as well as a strengthening won could ease concerns over inflation.

    While rapidly rising property prices could strengthen the case for a prolonged tightening cycle, Leather mentioned that the BOK was "more likely to favour macroprudential measures over further rate hikes to address its financial stability concerns.".

    After the decision, the country's benchmark Kospi rose 1.88%.

    Beware higher correlation but nab high U.S. credit yields, fund managers say

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (518 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The artificial intelligence boom could lead to a recession, whether through a collapse in AI investment or widespread job losses as the technology advances, a hedge fund manager said.
    • "I do worry that if we don't have an AI-led recession in a few years, we're going to have an unemployment-led recession," Sheru Chowdhry, founder and chief investment officer at DSC Meridian Capital, noted during a panel discussion moderated by CNBC's Joanna Ossinger at the iConnections Global Alts Asia conference in Singapore last week.
    • According to recent reports, chowdhry's warning highlights a risk that extends beyond a potential bursting of the AI bubble.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The artificial intelligence boom could lead to a recession, whether through a collapse in AI investment or widespread job losses as the technology advances, a hedge fund manager said.

    "I do worry that if we don't have an AI-led recession in a few years, we're going to have an unemployment-led recession," Sheru Chowdhry, founder and chief investment officer at DSC Meridian Capital, noted during a panel discussion moderated by CNBC's Joanna Ossinger at the iConnections Global Alts Asia conference in Singapore last week.

    According to recent reports, chowdhry's warning highlights a risk that extends beyond a potential bursting of the AI bubble. Rapid advances in the technology could lead to widespread job losses, with implications for the housing market and consumer spending, he stated.

    "If this continues to go at the pace it is, I think in a few years a lot of us will probably not have jobs," Chowdhry said, adding that investors would have to rethink their approach to sectors such as housing and discretionary spending.

    Even so, the fund manager remains bullish on computing power and sees opportunities in data centers, despite concerns about AI valuations.

    The current AI investment cycle reminds Chowdhry of the dot-com bubble and the telecommunications infrastructure buildout of the early 2000s.

    "This cycle reminds me of the dot-com bubble and the telecom build we had going on in the early 2000s," he stated. "Every cycle is different, but it kind of rhymes in some ways.".

    Chowdhry also questioned whether semiconductor companies could sustain their profit margins in the coming years.

    However, he sees opportunities in data centers, pointing to access to power and grid connections as major bottlenecks in the AI buildout.

    "If you can identify data centers, I feel like that's going to be the picks and shovels of this cycle," he said.

    In particular, data centers that can secure permits and access to power within the next two years present a significant investment opportunity, he added.

    In a recent development, beyond AI infrastructure, Chowdhry also pointed to attractive yields in U.S. credit markets.

    According to recent reports, he cited yields of around 8.5% on U.S. high-yield bonds and 9.5% on leveraged loans, describing the current market environment as an opportunity to "get paid to wait.".

    Sources indicate that investment portfolios may be more vulnerable to market volatility than they appear, according to Dan Gelernter, director of AI at R.G. Niederhoffer Capital Management, who spoke on the same panel.

    Average monthly correlations across investable assets rose from around 5% between the 1960s and 1990s to roughly 11% to 12% by 2020, according to research cited by Gelernter.

    His own analysis suggests that the figure has climbed further to around 15% to 16% in 2026.

    "Most portfolios are more highly levered, less liquid, more highly correlated than they appear to be, and that problem will get worse the more markets move," Gelernter said.

    Within the AI trade, Joo Kian Ong, a partner at AP3X Capital, remarked Samsung Electronics would be a good long position, with SK Hynix or Micron on the other side as potential shorts.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Inside India newsletter: Roaring economy, foreign investors’ return and now record auto sales

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1012 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from Singapore.
    • Welcome to the latest edition of "Inside India" — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy.
    • Industry observers note that despite 2026 being a challenging year with high global energy prices and supply chain disruptions, the Indian economy has fared surprisingly well.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from Singapore.

    Welcome to the latest edition of "Inside India" — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy.

    Industry observers note that despite 2026 being a challenging year with high global energy prices and supply chain disruptions, the Indian economy has fared surprisingly well. The auto industry, a key pillar of manufacturing and employment, has breached several records this year and is poised to report its best-ever sales.

    This week, I spoke to experts to decode what this stellar performance means for one of the world's most promising consumer markets.

    In a recent development, any thoughts on today's newsletter? Share them with the team.

    Industry observers note that india's economy expanded at 7.8% in the June quarter, beating expectations, even as growth in several major economies cooled. Foreign portfolio investors who had been exiting Indian markets in droves for most of the year have also started returning in historic numbers.

    In a recent development, and now, the world's third-largest auto market is set to for a record this year as better road connectivity, tax cuts, and easier financing options have fueled bumper sales over the last several months. That comes at a time when major auto markets across the world, from China to the U.S. have been seeing a slump in sales.

    "10 years ago, despite having the money, people did not buy cars, but now even if they don't have the money, they take financing and buy," Amar Sheth, vice president of the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations, told CNBC, pointing to the shift in consumer mindset.

    They are becoming "more optimistic" about the future and, rather than waiting, consumers are willing to take a loan and purchase something useful to them now, he adds.

    The industry body that Sheth represents mentioned on Monday that automakers in India were poised to sell more than 30 million vehicles in the financial year ending March 2027, dubbing the sector as a "reflection of the wider India growth story.".

    From April to October, total vehicle retail sales in India reached 18.7 million units, up 10% from a year earlier, with car, tractor and commercial vehicle sales growing more than 15%, as per FADA data.

    The optimism of the industry body is also shared by major automakers; several of whom have announced capacity expansion looks this year to meet the growing consumer demand.

    Japanese automakers Maruti Suzuki and Toyota plan to raise capacity by 1.2 million units and 200,000 units, while Korea's Hyundai Motors will add capacity for 150,000 units, as per data shared by automotive industry intelligence provider Mobility Global. Leading Indian companies Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra and JSW have also confirmed capacity addition looks, the data indicated.

    India is the only major auto market in the world that is growing while most others such as France, Germany, and Korea are "either declining or are flat," Puneet Gupta, director India and ASEAN at Mobility Global, told CNBC, explaining the reason behind car companies investing in the country.

    Gupta stated that the Chinese automotive market hit an inflection point in 2007, when the GDP per capita crossed $2,500, and now India is "at a similar point." He added that government support for the auto industry would be crucial in replicating the boom seen in the Chinese auto industry.

    The catalyst for India's auto sector boom traces back to last September, when the government confirmed a wide range of tax cuts to spur domestic consumption.

    The auto industry contributes 7.1% to the country's gross domestic product, 49% to manufacturing GDP, 15% to goods and services tax collection, and supports 30 million jobs, as per government data.

    While the tailwinds from the tax cuts have faded, experts now believe that replacement demand and the growing reach of financing options to smaller cities will unlock the next phase of growth.

    Consumption has been strong this year as the government has partly shielded people from rising energy costs while corporates, with their strong balance sheets, have been slow to pass on price hikes, Gaura Sengupta, chief economist at India's IDFC First Bank, remarked.

    So far this year, wage growth has been good, the labor market has held up equity markets haven't corrected sharply, keeping the wealth effect intact, she said, underscoring the reasons driving consumption along with easy access to credit.

    Despite the economy facing external shocks, producers are also "feeling confident to add capacity" as they have seen domestic demand sustain, Sengupta added.

    However, experts remarked that the central bank's recent tightening of monetary policy and price hikes by automakers could slightly take the edge off the auto sales boom in the last few months of the financial year.

    While urban demand is unlikely to get affected, rural sales growth could moderate, they added.

    "Overall retail should close FY27 in high single digits," Diwakar Murugan, senior automotive analyst at Omdia, told CNBC, adding that this year's record sales are not a one-time spike but a "structural reset.".

    China has changed tactics but is still thwarting India's rise, a U.S. panel saysChina is "actively working to suppress India's rise," even as the relationship between the two major Asian powers has thawed in the past year, according to a U.S. panel that sees an opening for greater outreach to India.

    Recent findings suggest that U.K.-India trade deal faces a stiff test over Scotch whisky import taxesWithin months of taking effect, the India-U.K. trade deal is facing an early test, as Upcoming Delhi resists extending preferential tariffs to bulk Scotch whisky imports.

    Industry observers note that investors give a thumbs down to Tata Steel-APL Apollo $1.67 billion deal, plunging sharesTata Steel, one of the world's leading steel producers, on Monday said it will buy a 26.4% stake in India's largest structural steel pipe and tube maker, APL Apollo, for 155.1 billion rupees ($1.67 billion). However, investors reacted negatively to the deal.

    According to recent reports, nov. 27: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO listing.

    North Korea's Kim calls for nuclear arsenal expansion, says status 'will never change'

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (465 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for bolstering the country's nuclear arsenal and expanding the use of tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains, state media reported Thursday, as Pyongyang reaffirmed its determination to retain its nuclear arms.
    • Kim's comments followed a working visit Wednesday to facilities involved in nuclear material production and weapons research, according to the Korean Central News Agency.
    • At the Nuclear Weapons Institute, he urged greater attention to "operationalizing" tactical nuclear weapons for a range of missions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for bolstering the country's nuclear arsenal and expanding the use of tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains, state media reported Thursday, as Pyongyang reaffirmed its determination to retain its nuclear arms.

    Kim's comments followed a working visit Wednesday to facilities involved in nuclear material production and weapons research, according to the Korean Central News Agency.

    At the Nuclear Weapons Institute, he urged greater attention to "operationalizing" tactical nuclear weapons for a range of missions.

    Kim directly linked the development of those weapons to North Korea "sharing a border with its most dangerous, hostile state," an apparent reference to South Korea.

    Industry observers note that the visit was part of Pyongyang's efforts to counter what Kim described as "the reckless expansion of adversary states' nuclear forces and military alliances," according to KCNA. He also singled out South Korea as a threat to North Korea's security and sovereignty.

    Kim reiterated that North Korea's status as a nuclear-armed state was irreversible, dismissing "denuclearization rhetoric" and saying its nuclear status "will never change.".

    "[Our nuclear policy] is a core element of safeguarding the sovereignty of the Republic, enshrined in the supreme law of the state," he added.

    The report did not identify the sites Kim visited or disclose any production figures.

    The announcement followed an assessment last week by the International Atomic Energy Agency that another extension to Yongbyon's original uranium-enrichment facility had been externally completed by late October.

    The nuclear watchdog has lacked access to North Korea since 2009 and monitors its activities using satellite imagery and open-source intelligence.

    It has been revealed that citing what he portrayed as growing threats from Washington and its allies, Kim accused the U.S. of encouraging neighboring allies to acquire nuclear-powered submarines, pursuing nuclear sharing and the joint use of nuclear weapons.

    His comments come after South Korea announced efforts to acquire nuclear-powered submarines after President Donald Trump backed the plan in October 2025, according to a White House joint fact sheet. Nuclear-powered propulsion does not itself mean that a vessel carries nuclear weapons.

    Trump had expressed interest in meeting with Kim at the APEC summit in Shenzhen last week, according to Reuters, but no meeting took place and North Korea did not publicly respond to the proposal.

    Trump denied that Kim had ignored him, adding that communications could "start up right away," in an interview with the Latest York Post Tuesday. He said the two leaders had not been in contact "recently.".

    "We've been off to other things," Trump added.

    Sources indicate that north Korea has continued to accelerate its nuclear weapons development and rebuff South Korean and U.S. attempts to resume dialogue since negotiations between Trump and Kim collapsed in 2019.

    — CNBC's Jenny Lee contributed to this report.

    • South Korean beauty stocks jumped Thursday as the country's skincare brands dominated Amazon's bestseller rankings ahead of Black Friday.
    • Shares of K-beauty giant APR climbed 3.77%, while cosmetic contracts manufacturers Kolmar Korea and Cosmax gained 5.46% and 2.91%, respectively.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    South Korean beauty stocks jumped Thursday as the country's skincare brands dominated Amazon's bestseller rankings ahead of Black Friday.

    Shares of K-beauty giant APR climbed 3.77%, while cosmetic contracts manufacturers Kolmar Korea and Cosmax gained 5.46% and 2.91%, respectively.

    APR shares, in particular, have rallied sharply this week, up 28%, defying a broader market sell-off in Seoul markets, with the benchmark Kospi index down 2.65% during the same period.

    A cosmetic sector index tracked by Meritz Securities had gained 12% this week until Wednesday, according to a Thursday note from the brokerage.

    According to recent reports, the rally reflects renewed optimism over earnings growth following strong performances by K-beauty brands across major e-commerce platforms in the U.S. and Europe with Black Friday sales already underway, as well as increasingly attractive valuations following months of share price declines, according to Meritz.

    Sources indicate that K-beauty products topped Amazon's skincare bestseller rankings across six major markets — the U.S., the U.K., Germany, France, Spain and Italy — as of Nov. 25, according to data compiled by Meritz Securities. Other Korean beauty brands, including Biodance, Illiyoon and Anua, also ranked among the top 10 in the U.S., the data showed.

    Industry observers note that as of Thursday morning, Korean beauty products occupied several of the top spots in Amazon's U.S. beauty and personal care category, the e-commerce website highlighted.

    Meritz Securities expects APR shares to maintain their positive momentum through the year-end, with a more substantial rebound in early 2027.

    The brokerage named APR and Cosmax as its top picks in the cosmetics sector. Korean beauty brands have established an "overwhelming presence" in the bestseller rankings of major e-commerce platforms during Black Friday sales, prompting the market to reassess the growth's potential, the brokerage noted.

    #199684. Latest Update: Robots could be doing household chores in just 1-2 years, Chinese EV firm states

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (704 w)
    📖 Baca
    EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Robots could be doing household chores in just 1-2 years, Chinese EV firm states

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (704 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • BEIJING — The household robot could soon become a reality, Brian Gu, co-president of Xpeng, a Chinese electric car company which has entered the humanoids space, told CNBC.
    • Recent findings suggest that "Maybe after successful deployment into commercial settings, maybe another one to two years, we can start thinking about deploying into home settings," Gu remarked.
    • According to recent reports, xpeng revealed its latest general-purpose humanoid robot Iron on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    BEIJING — The household robot could soon become a reality, Brian Gu, co-president of Xpeng, a Chinese electric car company which has entered the humanoids space, told CNBC.

    Recent findings suggest that "Maybe after successful deployment into commercial settings, maybe another one to two years, we can start thinking about deploying into home settings," Gu remarked. "Technology is moving at a much faster clip.".

    According to recent reports, xpeng revealed its latest general-purpose humanoid robot Iron on Wednesday. The company plans to start training the robot as a store assistant in its retail car locations in the first quarter next year, after starting mass production in January. Sales are set to begin in the second quarter, with deliveries expected later in the year.

    Founded in 2014 as an electric car manufacturer, Xpeng beat Tesla to rolling out driver-assist in mainland China. The Chinese automaker has launched its own artificial intelligence chips. It's also expanded into personal flying vehicles and robotics. The robotics unit this summer raised $900 million at a $6.3 billion valuation in its first funding round, led by IDG Capital.

    Industry observers note that investors, however, appear to be a tad skeptical about the developments at Xpeng, with the downturn in the Chinese auto market also weighing on the manufacturer. Xpeng's shares, listed in both Newly introduced York and Hong Kong, have dropped more than 55% this year amid broad sector declines.

    In a recent development, china's humanoid industry has faced more regulatory scrutiny on financing in recent months after Unitree's high-profile IPO and stock slump, as well as a rush of capital into the sector. That's all raised questions about commercialization and the efficacy of the core tech.

    It has been revealed that gu mentioned Xpeng's robotics stands out for its rare combination of the hardware, software and real-life use cases. He's expecting to add more investors after Iron's planned commercial launch next year.

    Sources indicate that "You can always make the head talk, you can always make the leg run, you can always make the hands to do certain tasks," Gu noted. "But doing a task while you're walking and answering questions at the same time, that's the most challenging part. And then doing everything well, not falling down, not getting distracted. The model has to work in sync.".

    Most humanoid robot startups, especially in China, focus on a portion of the tech, such as hands or the artificial intelligence-powered brain. Some in the industry also see themselves as original equipment manufacturers, with another company tying the parts together for the finished robot.

    But that may be easier remarked than done.

    According to recent reports, xpeng's co-founder and CEO He Xiaopeng, a software engineer, always thought that software could solve "everything,'" Gu said. "And after he got into the EV business he realized how hard it is to make hardware ... really do the things that you want to do safely and consistently.".

    On Wednesday, Xpeng unveiled its "Turing Physical AI Architecture" for using AI and real-time decision-making tech to control cars and humanoids.

    Gu told CNBC that Xpeng's robotics development only needs the driver-assist chips, which the company already has, indicating limited impact from U.S. restrictions on advanced Nvidia chip sales to China.

    "Right now we don't see any change to our supply chain, and also ability to have these chips.".

    In 2023, Xpeng's then-head of autonomous driving, Xinzhou Wu, left to lead Nvidia's automotive chip business.

    As Xpeng ramps up its humanoid robotics business, Gu mentioned the manufacturer's existing work in autonomous driving technology translates easily to a new product line — with far higher profit margins. "It's much easier to be profitable for the robotics business than the autos business.".

    According to recent reports, robotics will likely become a meaningful part of Xpeng's business in two to three years, Gu said, with profitability coming as soon as next year. That value will "dramatically" increase with robots entering households, he said.

    It has been revealed that but Gu noted that compared to commercial environments, homes require robots to act safely around elderly people, children and pets, in addition to reacting to emergency situations. That increases requirements for battery power and performance consistency, he noted.

    #199680. Judge blocks FCC early-renewal process for Disney-owned ABC stations, for now

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (400 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Judge blocks FCC early-renewal process for Disney-owned ABC stations, for now

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (400 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A judge has temporarily blocked the Federal Communications Commission from continuing its early renewal of a set of broadcast station licenses for Disney-owned ABC.
    • District Court in Washington granted Disney the preliminary injunction it sought and denied the FCC's attempt to dismiss the suit.
    • Sources indicate that "This is not a close case," wrote the federal judge.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A judge has temporarily blocked the Federal Communications Commission from continuing its early renewal of a set of broadcast station licenses for Disney-owned ABC.

    Judge Loren L. AliKhan of U.S. District Court in Washington granted Disney the preliminary injunction it sought and denied the FCC's attempt to dismiss the suit.

    Sources indicate that "This is not a close case," wrote the federal judge. "Given the extreme, indeed existential, nature of the possible penalty Plaintiffs face—loss of their broadcast licenses—the court concludes that early license renewal proceedings create a risk sufficient to chill a broadcaster of ordinary firmness.".

    In a recent development, the broadcast network had filed the lawsuit and followed the FCC beginning its early review of the ABC licenses. The government agency cited concerns around ABC's diversity, equity and inclusion efforts as the reason behind the start of the early renewal — years ahead of their scheduled expiration.

    "Today's decision is an key victory for the First Amendment," noted an ABC spokesperson.

    An FCC spokesperson said in a statement that the part of the decision granting ABC's motion "is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law," the Associated Press reported.

    In her ruling, AliKhan noted that early license renewal proceedings came over a year into the FCC's enforcement push against ABC, starting with an investigation into Disney's employment practices in March 2025 and leading to the renewal proceedings in April this year.

    ABC on Tuesday had said that it continued to "face irreparable harm" from the administration, which "has been acting" through the FCC, which is run by President Donald Trump appointee Brendan Carr.

    AliKhan, a Joe Biden appointee, noted in her ruling that ABC had to change how it handled guest appearances for top shows "The View" and "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" with no candidate for public office appearing on the former and a senatorial candidate's appearance on the latter uploaded to YouTube instead of being broadcast.

    "The prospect of license non-renewal has also factored into plaintiffs' calculus of when and how they cover President Trump and political topics," noted the judge.

    ABC had alleged that Trump and Carr have been making comments "intended to chill their protected speech," and that such comments have escalated since the 2024 presidential election.

    The White House and the FCC didn't immediately respond to requests for comment from CNBC.

    — CNBC's Dan Mangan contributed to the story.

    #199661. Tech Report: How Trump’s latest tariff moves hand India an edge over rival Asian exporters

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (466 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: How Trump’s latest tariff moves hand India an edge over rival Asian exporters

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (466 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the latest U.S.
    • The Office of the United States Trade Representative has proposed a tariff of 17% on Indian exports if New Delhi "were to reach an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade" with Washington.
    • Meanwhile, the USTR has proposed tariffs of 18% on Bangladesh, Cambodia, Thailand, and 20% on China and Vietnam, subject to their respective trade deals, handing India a competitive advantage over rival exporters.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the latest U.S. tariff rates announced Wednesday have signaled that Washington is willing to offer India an edge over its competitors if New Delhi agrees to finalize a long-pending trade deal.

    The Office of the United States Trade Representative has proposed a tariff of 17% on Indian exports if New Delhi "were to reach an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade" with Washington. It added that without a trade deal, India could face tariffs of up to 25% under Section 301 investigations encompassing excess production capacity that harms U.S. interests.

    Meanwhile, the USTR has proposed tariffs of 18% on Bangladesh, Cambodia, Thailand, and 20% on China and Vietnam, subject to their respective trade deals, handing India a competitive advantage over rival exporters.

    According to recent reports, the U.S. expects the announcement of a lower tariff rate will encourage New Delhi to sign off on a trade deal before the G20, Atman Trivedi, partner at Washington-based DGA Albright Stonebridge Group, told CNBC.

    India has got a "better bargain with Washington than its main competitors," and it may be enough for the Indian government "to declare victory and secure domestic backing for the deal," Trivedi remarked.

    In February, U.S. President Donald Trump had confirmed a deal with India, claiming that Fresh Delhi had accepted to "Buy American" at a much higher level after the U.S. agreed to slash tariffs to 18% from 50% earlier.

    It has been revealed that the India-U.S. trade deal has been pending with both sides indicating there was little room to grant concessions, while the Supreme Court annulling Trump tariffs allowed Fresh Delhi to demand preferential tariffs that give it an edge over competitors.

    "Today's announcement increases the urgency of reaching an agreement," Ronak D. Desai, visiting fellow at Hoover Institution, Stanford University, told CNBC. He added that while the prospect of a 17% tariff may strengthen the economic case for the deal, the threat of a 25% tariff could stir the sensitivity of the Indian government.

    "The Modi government will be particularly sensitive to any perception that India is conceding under American Pressure," Desai said.

    India's commerce ministry on Wednesday said it "does not have structural excess capacity in any sector," denying the findings of the USTR investigation, but added that it remains committed to "working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement.".

    Despite India facing steep tariffs, which were raised to 50%, Fresh Delhi's trade surplus with the U.S. rose to $57.3 billion in 2025 from $45.2 billion in 2024.

    Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Trump are likely to meet in December for the G20 leaders' meeting in Florida, and several experts believe the two leaders could seal the trade deal on the sidelines of the summit.

    #199653. Vance claims he was assured Jensen Huang was not under DOJ investigation

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (674 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Vance claims he was assured Jensen Huang was not under DOJ investigation

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (674 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Vice President JD Vance remarked Wednesday that Attorney General Todd Blanche told him Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not under investigation.
    • Industry observers note that "I was told by the Department of Justice and multiple officials in our national security apparatus that he was under no investigation," Vance told reporters in Ohio on Wednesday after being asked what assurances he had gotten that Huang was not under investigation.
    • Vance spoke two days after President Donald Trump told CNBC in an interview that an investigation had been done.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Vice President JD Vance remarked Wednesday that Attorney General Todd Blanche told him Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not under investigation.

    Industry observers note that "I was told by the Department of Justice and multiple officials in our national security apparatus that he was under no investigation," Vance told reporters in Ohio on Wednesday after being asked what assurances he had gotten that Huang was not under investigation. "Not even that he was about to be prosecuted; that he's under no investigation.".

    Vance spoke two days after President Donald Trump told CNBC in an interview that an investigation had been done.

    Trump was asked what Blanche had told him about potential criminal liability for Huang and the question of whether Nvidia chips had ended up in China in violation of U.S. export laws.

    "They did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he, himself, was exonerated," Trump said Monday.

    Reuters reported Wednesday that the Department of Justice did not conduct a formal investigation into Huang before Trump pushed for his reinstatement as CEO.

    Blanche had concluded there was no evidence Huang had broken any laws based on investigations into Nvidia clients Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed, according to the report.

    The DOJ did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Reuters report. And the White House didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on Vance saying Huang was under no investigation when Trump had noted there was one. Nvidia didn't immediately respond to a request for comment about Vance's remarks.

    Blanche on Tuesday dodged questions about whether there had been an investigation.

    "What the president noted is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him," Blanche said after being asked whether the DOJ had investigated Huang and, if so, what were the results of the probe.

    Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia on Monday, after the chipmaker's board of directors stated it had received "input from senior levels of the United States government" that Huang was not a national security risk. Trump took credit for Huang's reinstatement in the interview with CNBC shortly after Nvidia's announcement.

    Huang resigned following The Newly introduced York Times reporting multiple affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who is alleged to be a spy for Beijing and who was an executive for the Singapore-based cloud provider Megaspeed.

    Sources indicate that the reporting added fuel to allegations that Nvidia should have known its artificial intelligence chips were being diverted to China and being used by Chinese companies, violating U.S. export laws.

    "The product they create is a very vital part of us staying ahead of the SI arms race with China. We really do care about ensuring those chips do not fall into the wrong hands," Vance remarked, using the Trump administration's preferred acronym for AI, which the president calls "super intelligence.".

    "We actually see this is an opportunity for Nvidia to focus on complying with American export controls, and we think Jensen Huang is going to take that very seriously," Vance continued.

    "We received the assurances that he was not under any significant — he was under no investigation — and the accusations against him were based on anonymous reporting, not on actual evidence," Vance said.

    On Tuesday, Trump left the door open to pardon Huang in an interview with the Fresh York Post, but Vance said on Wednesday that the CEO doesn't need one.

    "I don't think he needs a pardon at all," Vance said. "I haven't seen any evidence again that he committed a crime. And if there is evidence that he committed a crime, then that's up to relevant authorities to actually bring a prosecution against him.".

    Huang is scheduled to appear for a closed-door interview with House committees about his dealings with Megaspeed on Tuesday. At the same time, Nvidia will hold its annual conference where it showcases newly introduced technology in Washington.

    — Kevin Breuninger contributed to this report.
